key_insight: High magnetic fields reveal chiral, enantiomer-dependent circularly polarized magneto-photoluminescence in 2D perovskites, indicating Rashba-driven exciton mixing and strong spin-selective emission.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify how chirality, spin splitting, and disorder suppression can be leveraged to tune optoelectronic emission in perovskite-based photonic and spintronic devices.
method: Measured circularly polarized magneto-photoluminescence (MPL) of R- and S-(C4H9NH3)2PbI4
Applied pulsed magnetic fields up to 50 T at 4.2 K
Compared field-dependent PL peak position, intensity, linewidth, and polarization channels
evidence_signal: The R-form showed strong preferential RC emission (I_RC/I_LC = 10:1), with opposite handedness in the S-form, plus field-driven intensity enhancement and linewidth narrowing.
watch_item: The measurements were performed at 4.2 K under extreme pulsed magnetic fields, so practical device translation may be limited by temperature and field requirements.
paper_title: Circularly Polarized Magneto-Photoluminescence in Two-Dimensional Chiral Perovskites R- and S-(C4H9NH3)2PbI4 under High Magnetic Fields
